_rules: Evidence level describes the fact, not the artifact. A claim printed in this repository's dossier is INTERNAL_PROJECT_HISTORY: the publication is verifiable, the claim is not.
No entry may be published as established fact while its evidence is NEEDS_VERIFICATION or UNCERTAIN.
Any timeframe with precision 'approx' must render its qualifier visibly in copy. Unknown dates remain unknown; they are not upgraded to approximate.
Prefer 'unknown' over 'probably', and 'not publicly available' over 'coming soon', wherever that is more accurate.
Internal engineering milestones are not converted into public marketing claims.
Ecosystem participation is never written as ownership or founding.
Employment is never presented as a personal project. Experiments are never presented as launched products.
Third-party personal information is not recorded in this file, even where it currently appears on the published site.
Where information is incomplete, use a controlled placeholder. Do not fill gaps with plausible guesses.

work.title: SWICE
work.summary: A personal AI OS with a deterministic financial execution subsystem. In development.

positioning.supplied: SWICE is a personal AI OS. Trading is one of the things SWICE can do — a capability and a subsystem, not the identity of the project.
positioning.de_emphasis: financial performance claims of any kind

timeframe.note: No start date supplied. Recorded as current and in development.

components._note: Supplied as work that has been carried out. Some items are INTERNAL PROJECT HISTORY. Public disclosure of any individual item requires confirmation that it is appropriate to disclose, including whether internal architecture names may be published at all.

internal_progress._note: Internal engineering progress exists and has been supplied privately. Because this file lives in a public repository, the specific values are deliberately NOT restated here — the same discipline applied to the removed private assets. A test-suite count and an internal phase label are engineering facts about a private codebase, not product achievements, and publishing either would invite readers to infer maturity that has not been claimed.
withheld: an internal phase label for the execution engine (label withheld)

internal_architecture_names._note: At least one internal architecture component has a project name that has not been cleared for public disclosure. The name is deliberately not recorded in this file, because this repository is public and recording it here would publish it. It is held privately until Bobbi Andrea confirms whether it may be named. The same applies to any private infrastructure detail, credential, secret, private endpoint, wallet detail or API key.

items: It is not publicly available as a finished consumer product.
It is not a live-money trading service.
Trading is currently associated with deterministic execution infrastructure, experimentation, testing, and paper-mode development.
Live trading has not been represented as launched.

media.note: No screenshots or demo material. Any asset must be checked for secrets before use.

must_not_claim: performance results presented as public product performance
that it is a commercially deployed autonomous financial product
confirmation_required: Whether the internal architecture component name held privately may be published
Which of the sixteen components above may be described publicly, and in how much detail
Start date, and whether development has been continuous
Whether any repository, demo or screenshot exists that contains no secrets
Final public status wording
work.notes: Flagship technical case study, and the marker of the transition into deeper software and AI engineering — a progression, not a replacement of the earlier creative, design, radio and Web3 history. No evidence exists anywhere in this repository; every fact is supplied. The framing correction matters: an earlier reading treated this as a trading project, and it is not. Trading is one subsystem of a personal AI OS. The case study should lead with architecture and engineering practice — paper trading, shadow mode, transaction simulation, chaos and failure testing, architecture governance — because that is what demonstrates the engineering without making any claim about money.
